html:
SMTO-FIL-0044 — The copy tried to finish before the whole file arrived

GUID: 1adeef67-ed22-46a9-b591-188c1702fb37
Slug: file-transfer-size-mismatch
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • At the end of a copy between Gateways, the receiving computer had less data than the file's full size. SMTO did not put the incomplete file in place at the destination.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, use Check connection on both Gateways, and use Check for updates if either is out of date. A dropped connection or a version difference can leave part of the file unsent.
  2. Ask SMTO in the conversation to show the size and last-modified time of the file at the destination and of the original file, and compare them. If the destination file is already there and matches, the copy doesn't need to be repeated.
  3. If the destination file is missing or still the old version, ask SMTO to copy it again. A new copy sends the whole file from the start.

What success looks like

  • The new copy finishes and SMTO reports the file was copied and verified.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateways. Don't keep repeating the copy if it stops the same way; the Gateways need to be checked first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • destination_commit was requested while the session's accepted byte offset did not equal the size declared at destination_begin, so the stage was neither hashed nor published.

What this means

  • Destination commit was requested before received offset equalled the session's declared total size. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Destination commit was requested before received offset equalled the session's declared total size.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare accepted offset and declared size; publication has not passed this commit precondition.

How to fix it

  • Query destination_status for bytes_received versus the declared size, and check whether a write was lost or the controller and Gateway versions disagree on chunk accounting. Abort or settle the original stage, confirm cleanup, and start a new copy instead of committing a partial stage.
  • Inspect the original transfer's accepted bytes and settle or continue it through the supported protocol before committing.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The owned stage has the verified complete size and matching hash before any publication.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
